rationale:
Quota today: 1 long-form, 3 Shorts, 0 carousels.

**L1 (Lane A).** Today has no qualifying Lane C news. TRANSCEND-T2D-2 is a topline that already had a Short this week, and ATTAIN-J's topline was public earlier. So the long-form goes to the next practical tirzepatide topic still open in the queue: constipation and fibre. "Stopping tirzepatide" ran on 10-27, so it's inside the 30-day window. Hair loss is on the 10-30 covered list, and its redo stays with the owner and EIC rather than being re-planned here. Constipation is one of the most searched side effects and is fully covered by the FDA label, the SURMOUNT-1 tables and the 2025 joint nutrition advisory. That makes it an evergreen deep-dive that can pass the fact-check. It joins the Life on Tirzepatide cluster, where suggested-video traffic brings about 70% of Lane A minutes.

**Shorts.** Three topics on three different body systems: brain/mood, a weight-loss pill, and the gut.
- **08:00:** a calm "honest uncertainty" Short on tirzepatide and mood. It's an emerging topic with three new papers this week and few calm creators covering it. It's marked caution, so the angle is evidence-first and includes a support line.
- **13:00:** ATTAIN-J, orforglipron's newly peer-reviewed third Phase 3 trial (Oct 30). This is a deliberate exception to the 13:00 list:
  - Retatrutide's TRANSCEND-T2D-2 already had a Short this week (dysesthesia, 10-29).
  - A tirzepatide-vs-insulin head-to-head would run back-to-back with the same template as SURPASS-3 on 10-30.
  - ATTAIN-J is a fresh randomized fact, and the Short can feed our orforglipron long-form, which earns 202 minutes.
- **20:00:** the funnel Short, a spin-off of L1. It asks a new question: why piling on fibre fast can backfire. It closes with the verified-link line.

**Mix.** Rising/emerging: 2. Evergreen with a timely hook: 1. Myth-bust: 1. No carousels. Every piece carries "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line. The stopping and side-effect pieces also carry the don't-stop line.

pieces.topic: Tirzepatide constipation: how common it was in the trials vs placebo, why it happens (slower gut movement and eating and drinking less), and a food-first plan (fluids, fibre built up gradually, movement, routine), plus when to call your prescriber
pieces.angle:
Lane A (log 'lane: A'). Put it in the 'Life on Tirzepatide' playlist, 8–12 min, 14:00 ET.

Opening: the first spoken sentence answers the title with a 'you' scenario, e.g. 'Feeling backed up on tirzepatide? You're not alone. Constipation was one of the most common side effects in the trials, and a few simple, steady habits are what experts recommend.'

Chapters, named after searched questions:
(1) How common is constipation on tirzepatide? Use SURMOUNT-1 per-arm rates vs placebo, with group sizes and 72 weeks. Population: adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes. Fact-checker: confirm the 11.7% / 16.8% / 17.1% vs 5.8% figures against NEJM 2022 and the current Zepbound label, which was revised 28 Aug 2026. Add one SURPASS line, labelled 'type 2 diabetes'.
(2) Why does it happen? Use the label's wording that tirzepatide can delay gastric emptying. Smaller meals and lower fluid intake are a leading explanation, not a certainty.
(3) Does fibre help or hurt? Build fibre up gradually and pair it with fluids. Quote the advisory's 'avoiding fatty or high fiber foods during the first few days of treatment' only at that exact scope (easing nausea), and explain why it doesn't conflict.
(4) How much should I drink? Sip through the day, unless you've been told to limit fluids.
(5) Does movement help? A walk and a regular routine are our own tips, with no source tag.
(6) What about laxatives or supplements? Ask your pharmacist or prescriber before using any. No product names or doses.
(7) When to call your prescriber? Use the label's warning signs in its exact wording: severe stomach pain that won't go away, and vomiting or diarrhoea with signs of dehydration. Add 'contact your healthcare provider'.

All habits are 'recommended', never 'proven on tirzepatide'.

Re-hook every 45–75 s. One subscribe ask, after the 'what helps' payoff. Include 'Not personal advice', 'don't stop, switch or change your medicines on your own' and the full prescriber line. No dosing or titration talk, and no spoken titles.

Ending: 'There's a video I'd watch next, linked in the description.' The publisher links 'What to Eat on Tirzepatide'.

Thumbnail: before-after layout, 4 words or fewer (e.g. 'Gut Back on Track'), one labelled, relieved tummy character.
pieces.why: Next Lane A topic in the queue ('fibre and constipation'). It's a very common side effect with high search demand, it rests on the label, the trial data and the advisory, and it strengthens the Life on Tirzepatide suggested-video cluster.

pieces.topic: Do tirzepatide and other GLP-1 medicines affect mood or anxiety? New neuropsychiatric safety review (Rambam Maimonides Med J, Oct 26, 2026), the Medicare cohort (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 25), and a semaglutide panic-attack pharmacovigilance study with a notoriety-bias check (Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf, Nov 2026)
pieces.angle: Calm 'honest uncertainty' Short built on two anchors. (1) FDA Drug Safety Communication, 13 Jan 2026 (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-communications/fda-requests-removal-suicidal-behavior-and-ideation-warning-glucagon-peptide-1-receptor-agonist-glp): the FDA asked for the suicidal-thoughts warning to be removed from the Zepbound, Wegovy and Saxenda labels after its review of 91 placebo-controlled trials found no increased risk of suicidal thoughts or other psychiatric side effects. (2) The Oct 2026 Rambam review, which covers GLP-1 medicines and tirzepatide, using its conclusion wording verbatim. Optional third line, only if words allow: a semaglutide panic-attack reporting study found that reports jumped after 2023 media and regulatory attention, which is consistent with notoriety bias, so a reporting signal isn't proof of cause. Label it semaglutide and FAERS. Drop the Medicare cohort unless content_check confirms its findings and drug scope. Required lines: 'Everyone's different. If your mood changes on any medicine, tell your prescriber.' The crisis line: 988 in the US, Samaritans 116 123 in the UK, or local emergency services. 'Don't stop or change your medicines on your own.' 'Not personal advice.' Plus the full prescriber line. Title: 'Tirzepatide and Mood: What the Evidence Shows'. No #semaglutide unless the panic-attack line stays, and no emoji.
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide and Mood: What the Evidence Shows #shorts
pieces.why: Body-worry honest-uncertainty format (proven, median ~104), tirzepatide-first title, three fresh papers within a week, and low competition from calm sources. Brain topic adds body-system variety. | fact-check: All three cited sources exist. (a) Jani et al., 'Neuropsychiatric Safety of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists and Tirzepatide in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus or Obesity', Rambam Maimonides Med J 17(4), Oct 2026, https://www.rmmj.org.il/issues/73/articles/4883. I couldn't retrieve the conclusion text, so content_check must quote it from the PDF. (b) Baik et al., Diabetes Obes Metab, Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, observational, https://dom-pubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/dom.71459. The publisher returned 403, so confirm the findings and whether tirzepatide was even included. If it wasn't, call it 'GLP-1 medicines' only. (c) Melamed et al., Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf 2026, https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/pds.70517. FAERS 2018Q1–2024Q4, active comparators dulaglutide and empagliflozin. The crude semaglutide–panic attack signal weakened after adjustment, was not significant before the July 2023 regulatory communication, then rose in a pattern consistent with notoriety bias. Problems: three studies, a crisis line and three safety lines won't fit in 170 words. More importantly, the angle leaves out the strongest, most relevant dated fact. On 13 Jan 2026 the FDA asked for the suicidal behaviour and ideation warning to be removed from the Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels after a review found no increased risk (a meta-analysis of 91 placebo-controlled trials, 107,901 patients). The tone must stay 'honest uncertainty', not 'all clear'. Individual mood changes still matter and should be reported.

pieces.topic: Orforglipron's third Phase 3 trial, now peer-reviewed: ATTAIN-J in Japanese adults with obesity disease (238 randomized, 72 weeks, double-blind vs placebo; Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol, Oct 30, 2026)
pieces.angle: Title: 'Orforglipron Pill: What the Japan Trial Confirms'. Open within 10 s: 'In a 72-week trial in Japanese adults with obesity disease, orforglipron cut weight by up to 8.7% on average, compared with 0.6% on placebo.' Then give each arm with its n (6 mg −5.9%, n=61; 12 mg −8.7%, n=57; 36 mg −7.9%, n=60; placebo −0.6%, n=60), and say plainly that the highest dose didn't give the most loss. Use the measure the paper names. Define obesity disease: BMI 27 or higher plus type 2 diabetes, high blood pressure or high cholesterol. Add one line on why this matters: in many Asian populations, obesity-related conditions show up at lower BMI. Add ATTAIN-1 (12.4% vs 0.9%, if everyone stayed on treatment, adults without diabetes, 72 weeks), marked 'separate trials, not head-to-head'. US status: FDA approved 1 Apr 2026 for chronic weight management. Give the Japan or EU status only if verified on publish day. Add one per-arm nausea line from the paper. Close with the don't-switch line, 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line. Never call it the 'third' Phase 3 trial.
pieces.working_title: Orforglipron Pill: What Its Third Phase 3 Trial Confirms #shorts
pieces.why: The full paper came out Oct 30 and pill interest is rising. This deliberately replaces the 13:00 retatrutide/head-to-head slot: TRANSCEND-T2D-2 already had a Short this week, and an insulin head-to-head would repeat the 10-30 template. It can feed the orforglipron long-form (202 min). | fact-check: ATTAIN-J exists. It was published in Lancet Diabetes Endocrinol (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/landia/article/PIIS2213-8587(26)00232-9/abstract; registry NCT05931380, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05931380). Design: 238 randomized 1:1:1:1 (6 mg n=61, 12 mg n=57, 36 mg n=60, placebo n=60). Population: Japanese adults with obesity disease, defined as BMI ≥27 with type 2 diabetes, hypertension or dyslipidaemia. At 72 weeks, weight change was −5.9% / −8.7% / −7.9% vs −0.6% on placebo. Three issues. (1) The top dose did not give the largest loss: 12 mg (−8.7%) beat 36 mg (−7.9%). Leading with 'the top dose arm' would hide that and imply a dose-response the trial didn't show. Report all three arms, or say 'up to 8.7% with the 12 mg dose'. (2) 'Third Phase 3 trial' is not accurate. Orforglipron already has several peer-reviewed Phase 3 trials (ACHIEVE-1, ATTAIN-1, ATTAIN-2, ACHIEVE-J and others). Drop 'third' from the title and script. (3) I could not confirm the 30 Oct online date or which estimand the headline uses (the publisher returned 403). Content_check must confirm both before the '48 h / fresh' framing is used. Also, ATTAIN-1's 12.4% vs 0.9% is the 'if everyone stayed on treatment' figure (36 mg, adults without diabetes, 72 weeks), so label it that way and match the ATTAIN-J measure, or state that the measures differ. Verified US status: FDA approved Foundayo (orforglipron) for chronic weight management on 1 Apr 2026. The loop and 'what's confirmed?' format is fine. Avoid the dose numbers being heard as dosing advice: say 'three doses tested' and present them only as trial arms.

pieces.topic: Constipated on tirzepatide? Why piling on fibre all at once can backfire, and the 'slow fibre plus fluids' approach
pieces.angle: Title: 'Tirzepatide Constipation: Why Fibre Too Fast Can Backfire'. Opening: 'Backed up on tirzepatide, so you load up on fibre all at once? Adding a lot quickly can make bloating and discomfort worse. General constipation advice, like the NHS's, is to build fibre up gradually and drink fluids with it.' Then give one SURMOUNT-1 arm vs placebo, copied from L1's verified script. Add the advisory's 'first few days' high-fibre note, framed as being about nausea. Fluids: 'unless your doctor has told you to limit fluids'. Ask your pharmacist or prescriber before using any laxative, with no product names. Red flag, in label wording: severe stomach pain that won't go away means contact your healthcare provider. Then the don't-stop line, 'Not personal advice' and the prescriber line. Last line: 'Full breakdown on our channel, link in the description.'
pieces.working_title: Tirzepatide Constipation: Why More Fibre Can Backfire #shorts
pieces.why: Spin-off of L1: the funnel Short that sends people to today's Lane A long-form. It's a myth-bust hook with a tirzepatide-first title. | fact-check: This is a good funnel spin-off with a distinct question. The claim is well supported as general advice: NHS and NIDDK constipation guidance says to increase fibre gradually and drink fluids, because a sudden increase can cause gas and bloating. But it isn't tirzepatide-specific evidence, so attribute it to general constipation advice, not to 'experts' and not to tirzepatide trials. The working title 'Why More Fibre Can Backfire' could be heard as 'fibre is bad', when the video's message is 'too much, too fast'. Tighten it so the payoff matches. The SURMOUNT-1 number must match L1's verified figures exactly (arm, n, placebo, no diabetes, 72 weeks). Keep the advisory's high-fibre note at its exact scope: the first few days of treatment, to ease nausea.
